solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Caresser — one very quiet in such a naughty game!

indicators.note: the one and the very quiet sign are placed inside the word for a caresser

parts.note: someone who strokes is a stroker
the Roman numeral for one is I
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about a flirt keeping very quiet during a risqué game.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game where losers remove clothing is a classic naughty party game.

clue.text: Weapon depot destroyed when invaded by soldiers

indicators.note: invading troops get inside, so the soldiers go into the scrambled depot
something destroyed is wrecked and its letters rearranged

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A weapons store is wrecked when troops storm it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' looks like part of the story but is the anagram signal, and 'when invaded by' means the troops end up inside the jumbled store.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater missile is a naval weapon.

clue.text: Country home a detective probes

indicators.note: a probing detective pokes inside, so DI goes into the other letters

parts.note: to be at home is to be in
DI is Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective investigates a house in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A large nation of South Asia, so an example of a country.

clue.text: Turning up, thrusting type accounts for one easily defeated

indicators.note: turning the little word up round makes it read backwards

parts.note: someone who pushes and thrusts is a shover

explanation.surface: An aggressive go-getter turns out to be a soft touch after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses UP to PU; 'accounts for' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft touch or easy opponent is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: Refuse to get ruffled? You may not if losing at 1!

definitions.meaning: an idiomatic plea to stay calm and not lose your temper

definitions.text: You may not if losing at 1!
definitions.meaning: a loser at the game of 1 across must take off clothes, so the top comes off

explanation.walkthrough: The second half refers to 1 Across, a game where losing hands cost you garments.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stay calm; literally, losers at that game do not keep their tops on.

clue.text: Engineers left, making a noise

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Army engineers departed, creating a racket as they went.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud bang, such as a gunshot, is called this, so it is a noise.

clue.text: He-man? Not rector, primarily in the pulpit

indicators.note: not having something means that piece is removed from the word

parts.note: Rambo is the musclebound film hero, a macho he-man

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the leading letter of rector counts

explanation.surface: A macho figure appears in church, where the rector is not preaching.
explanation.walkthrough: The film character's name loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised reading desk or stand in early churches, a kind of pulpit.

clue.text: Loose morals with you acting in flirtatious manner?

indicators.note: loose letters are freed to be rearranged
the letters perform in a new role, another sign of rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone with lax morals playing up to you seems to be flirting.
explanation.walkthrough: MORALS and YOU together are rearranged; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave lovingly or with romantic intent is to act flirtatiously.

clue.text: Prejudice gets grand Tory looking silly

parts.note: grand means big

indicators.note: a word looking silly is in disarray, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bias is evident when an important Conservative makes a fool of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking silly' rearranges TORY into OTRY; a Tory is a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Intolerant bias towards others is a synonym for prejudice.

clue.text: Pressure brought with stick?

parts.note: P is the scientific symbol for pressure
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: Coercion applied using a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A poke with a pointed stick, used to urge someone on, applies pressure.

clue.text: Drunken peer in Berks town to stay out all night?

indicators.note: the jumbled nobleman goes inside the town name

parts.note: Slough is a town in Berkshire, a county west of London

indicators.note: drunken letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy aristocrat in a commuter town fails to get home overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: To bed down outdoors without shelter is to spend the night out in the open.

clue.text: Ice cream terribly elongated, end out of sight

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters come out in a muddled order
the letters of the word end disappear from the mix

explanation.surface: An ice cream stretched out so much that its end can no longer be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Take E, N, D away from ELONGATED, leaving LOGATE, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian-style ice cream, denser than the usual kind, so an ice cream by name.

clue.text: Youngsters including a jolly lot in IOW town

indicators.note: the youngsters hold the other pieces inside them

parts.note: youth is a collective word for young people
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, so the Royal Marines, RM

explanation.surface: A group of teenagers with cheerful companions in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: IOW is the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A small port on the Isle of Wight's north-west coast bears this name.

clue.text: Philosopher gets stuff for the match, having taken time off

indicators.note: taken off means removed from the word

parts.note: a bride's trousseau is the clothes and linen gathered for her wedding

explanation.surface: A thinker gathers equipment for a sporting fixture after taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' means a wedding, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques, the Genevan writer of The Social Contract, was an Enlightenment philosopher.

clue.text: African party overwhelmed by harsh division

indicators.note: being overwhelmed puts the party inside the other word

parts.note: severe means harsh
the ANC is the African National Congress of South Africa

explanation.surface: A political party in Africa is crushed by a bitter split.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting off or parting is a separation, a division.

clue.text: Whence cometh rain to east of the island

parts.note: rain falls from the sky

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding line about weather coming in east of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest Inner Hebridean isle, off Scotland's west coast, is an island.

clue.text: Indians in the distance? Careful!

indicators.note: the people are placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: dist. is the abbreviation for distance
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A warning that Native Americans are visible far off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being discreet means being circumspect and prudent, so careful.

clue.text: Wide boy gives bigwigs a going over

indicators.note: going over turns the word end over end, reading it backwards

parts.note: VIPs are very important people, bigwigs

explanation.surface: A shady character beats up some important people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wide boy' is British slang for a small-time crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashy petty dealer in black-market goods, a wheeler-dealer.

clue.text: Friend in excellent hospital — operation about to come up

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned operation surrounds the others
in a down answer coming up reads bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI
san is short for sanatorium, a hospital

explanation.surface: A pal is in a first-rate hospital with surgery imminent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' reverses OP to PO, which goes round AISAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word, from Italian and Spanish, for a fellow countryman or pal.

clue.text: Carts reversing outside joint where craftspeople work

indicators.note: the turned carts go outside the joint
the carts word is read backwards

parts.note: drays are heavy carts
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Carts back up outside a pub where artisans labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a pub, but here it is a body part; 'reversing' turns the carts round before they wrap it.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard where shipwrights build and repair vessels is a place of skilled work.

clue.text: Sir Thomas provides opportunities for some to get prizes

definitions.meaning: Sir Thomas Stamford ..., founder of modern Singapore

definitions.text: opportunities for some to get prizes
definitions.meaning: lotteries in which tickets are drawn for prizes

explanation.surface: A knight hands out chances to win prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonial founder's surname, and plural lotteries where ticket holders win prizes.

clue.text: Headache sets Margaret on edge

parts.note: Meg is a short form of Margaret
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A headache makes Margaret feel tense.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for migraine, so a severe headache.

clue.text: PM getting ennobled is earl, I'd fancy

indicators.note: fancy letters are arranged in an elaborate new way

explanation.surface: A prime minister made a peer; a nobleman fancies it.
explanation.walkthrough: The PM became Earl of Beaconsfield in 1876.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin, the Victorian Conservative prime minister, was raised to the peerage.

clue.text: Copper and gentleman no longer in contact

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a toff is an upper-class gentleman

explanation.surface: A policeman and a posh man have lost touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being isolated or disconnected means having no communication.

clue.text: Drum — something prohibited, not quite right

indicators.note: not quite means falling short by a final letter

parts.note: a taboo is something forbidden

explanation.surface: A drum is banned, and that is not quite fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A small medieval drum played with a pipe is a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Turned out to enter after-hours high-street establishment?

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes into the word for after hours

parts.note: late means after normal hours

indicators.note: out means awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People were kicked out on entering a late-night shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' reads as one phrase but splits: 'out' scrambles the first word, and 'to enter' puts that jumble inside the word for after hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service shop with coin washing machines, typical of a British high street.

clue.text: One should maybe beware of this nonsense

definitions.text: One should maybe beware of this
definitions.meaning: field signs warn walkers to beware of the male cow

explanation.surface: A warning about something risky, dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dangerous male bovine on warning signs, and slang for rubbish talk.

clue.text: Drill — something tedious

definitions.meaning: to drill is to make a hole
a dull, wearisome thing or person

explanation.definitionFit: To drill a hole and something dull are both senses of this word.

clue.text: Economist is absorbed by painter and his work

parts.note: Claude Monet, the French Impressionist

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken inside

parts.note: a painter's work is art

explanation.surface: An economist is engrossed by an artist and his paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: An economist who believes in controlling the money supply follows monetarism.
